title: Clean up a mailing list typed in by hand
examObjective: Applying correct syntax to write DataWeave transformations to coerce, format, order, and filter data
basics: `trim(s)` removes spaces from both ends of a String, and `lower(s)` turns it to lower case. They are ordinary functions, so they nest: `lower(trim(s))`. Cleaning text usually means applying a few of these in the right order.
prompt:
Sign-ups from a paper form were typed into a spreadsheet and arrive as an array of Strings. Before loading them into the mail platform:

- remove leading and trailing spaces,
- make every address lower case,
- drop any entry that is blank.

A blank entry may be an empty String or may be nothing but spaces. Keep the order of the rest.
hints: Two jobs: change each entry, then drop some. Decide which has to happen first.
Is `"   "` empty? Ask the engine with `isEmpty("   ")`.
Trim first, then filter on the trimmed value. An entry of spaces only becomes "" after trimming.
solution:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
---
payload map lower(trim($)) filter not isEmpty($)

mustFail.why: filters before trimming, so an entry of only spaces is not empty yet and survives as ""
mustFail.script:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
---
payload filter not isEmpty($) map lower(trim($))

mustFail.why: lower-cases but never trims, so addresses keep their stray spaces
mustFail.script:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
---
payload map lower($) filter not isEmpty(trim($))

explanation.approach: Order matters. A String of spaces is not empty, so it passes an `isEmpty` check until it has been trimmed. Clean every entry first, then filter on the cleaned values.

snippets.label: Spaces are not empty
snippets.note: Only after trimming does it count as blank.

snippets.label: Filtering first
snippets.script:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
---
payload filter not isEmpty($) map lower(trim($))
snippets.note: The spaces-only entry slipped through and came out as an empty String.
